claims.description: If another configured voter has actually won a newer-term majority election before VerifyLeader is invoked on L, and L does not reacquire authority during that operation, completed VerifyLeader must not return success based solely on a held reply produced before that election.

scope.description: Bounded verification API result after same-history replacement election; initial static leader/configuration fixture and controlled worker scheduling.
assumptions: Initial L term-7 leader with matching static three-voter configuration is a permitted prefix.
Crash-only delays/partition; no forged vote or heartbeat response.
No L reacquisition or configuration changes during the operation.

claims.source: Candidate derived from attributed implementation responsibilities

grounding.derivation: VerifyLeader is specified to ensure the peer is still leader and prevent stale data after leadership loss. Under a static three-voter configuration, actual election of F in term 8 by its own vote and N vote before invocation means L in term 7 cannot validly confirm continued authority during this operation absent reacquisition. Therefore a completed verification on L must not report success solely on an earlier term-7 reply. This is a necessary negative condition in the observed replacement-election context, not a requirement for all replies to be fresh or for verification eventually to complete.
grounding.applicability: Fixed voters L,F,N; pre-vote disabled for the replacement election; no L reelection, configuration change or newer reply during the verification interval; delayed genuine F response.
unresolved: Initial L leader state and committed configuration are fixtures; startup/election prefix not executed.
Ordinary replication and full runLeader setup are omitted; the controlled window represents their delay, without claiming all production schedules admit it.
Application reads and committed-log safety are excluded.
alternatives: Newer responses or incoming RPCs could step L down; those are absent in this selected schedule.
Pending verification is allowed. The oracle does not require eventual failure or success.
